author: Good Enough
description:
Patients were strapped down and left unable to move, for hours, sometimes even days.

In early insane asylums, the “tranquilizing chair” was used as a form of treatment, where patients were tightly restrained to stop all movement. Doctors believed that by keeping the body completely still, blood would be redirected to the brain and cure mental illness.

This video explores one of the most disturbing practices in medical history and what patients were forced to endure inside these institutions.
